# logfire_group_mappings (Resource)

Manages the identity-provider group mapping of a self-hosted Logfire instance. The mapping assigns organization and project roles to the members of identity-provider groups at their next sign-in. The instance has one mapping, so declare this resource once. It conflicts with the Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping`, which overrides the mapping that the API stores. The provider credential must be an API key from the admin organization with the `instance:admin` scope (`organization:admin` is equivalent).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Map identity-provider groups to organization and project roles. The provider
# credential must be an API key from the admin organization with the
# `instance:admin` scope. Do not set the Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping`
# on the same instance.
resource "logfire_organization" "team_a" {
  name = "team-a"
}

resource "logfire_group_mappings" "this" {
  mapping = [
    {
      group_id = "team-a-admins"
      organization_roles = [
        { organization = logfire_organization.team_a.name, role = "admin" },
      ]
    },
    {
      group_id = "platform-ops"
      organization_roles = [
        {
          # The organization and its project must already exist.
          organization = "platform"
          role         = "guest"
          project_roles = [
            { project = "api", role = "read" },
          ]
        },
      ]
    },
  ]
}
```

## Conflict with the Helm value

The Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping` overrides the mapping that the API stores.
While it is set, sign-in and SCIM group updates ignore this resource. Create fails
before it writes, because it reads `api_mapping_status` first. Update and destroy
fail on the 409 that the API answers to a write. A refresh warns and sets
`api_mapping_status` to `overridden_by_environment`. Remove the Helm value to manage
the mapping with Terraform.

## When the mapping applies

The mapping applies at each user's next sign-in. A SCIM group `PATCH` that adds or
removes a member applies the mapping to that member at once. For every organization
and project that it lists, the change adds, changes, or removes the user's access to
match the user's identity-provider groups. When several groups grant a role in the
same scope, the most permissive role applies. Membership in a user's own personal
organization is never removed. Neither a sign-in nor a SCIM update removes the last
admin of an organization or lowers that admin's role. The instance skips that change
and logs a warning. Organizations that the mapping does not list stay unchanged. In a
listed organization, sign-in manages only the projects listed in `project_roles`,
with one exception. When a sign-in removes the user from a listed organization, it
also removes all of the user's project memberships in that organization, including
projects that `project_roles` does not list.

## Role names are not validated

The API does not check role names. A wrong name gives no error. The sign-in skips
the role and the instance writes a warning to its log. The provider cannot check
names either, because roles belong to each organization. Compare each name with
the roles of its organization or project. Organizations and projects must exist,
and the API answers a missing name with a 400.

## Create, update, and destroy

Create reads the stored mapping first. It fails when the instance already stores a
mapping, so Terraform does not replace access rules that someone else wrote. The API
itself would accept the write, so this check belongs to the provider. Import the stored
mapping, copy it into the configuration, and apply. Import it the same way after a
create that failed once the instance had stored the mapping.

To move the resource to another address, use a `moved` block. Without one, Terraform
destroys the old address, which stores an empty mapping, and creates the new one in the
same apply. The create fails if it runs before the destroy, and the next apply stores
the mapping again.

Create and update replace the whole mapping, in the order of the list. The API has
no version and no lock, so when two writers update the mapping, the last write wins.
Declare this resource in one Terraform configuration per instance. The provider
cannot detect a second declaration in another configuration or workspace. The create
check sees only what is stored when it runs, so two declarations that create before
either stores a mapping both pass it. After that, each apply replaces the other's
mapping, and the last apply wins.

Destroy stores an empty mapping. It stops managing the scopes that the mapping
listed. It does not restore access that earlier sign-ins changed or removed.

## Requirements

This resource is only available on self-hosted deployments. It needs Logfire
v2026-07-22.02 or newer (Helm chart logfire-0.13.36 or newer), the first release
that reports `api_mapping_status` and answers 409 while the Helm value overrides
the API. The provider credential is an API key from the admin organization with
the `instance:admin` scope. The equivalent `organization:admin` scope also works.

## Schema

### Required

- `mapping` (Attributes List) The complete mapping, in the order that the instance stores it. An empty list stores no mapping. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mapping))

### Read-Only

- `api_mapping_status` (String) `active` when sign-in uses the stored mapping. `overridden_by_environment` when the Helm value `groupOrganizationMapping` is set, which makes the stored mapping unused.
- `id` (String) Always `instance`.

<a id="nestedatt--mapping"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mapping`

Required:

- `group_id` (String) The identity-provider group ID. Each group ID appears once.
- `organization_roles` (Attributes List) The roles that members of the group get in organizations. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mapping--organization_roles))

<a id="nestedatt--mapping--organization_roles"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mapping.organization_roles`

Required:

- `organization` (String) The organization name. The organization must exist.
- `role` (String) The built-in or custom organization role name. The API does not check it, so a wrong name gives no error and sign-in skips the role.

Optional:

- `project_roles` (Attributes List) The roles that members of the group get in projects of this organization. Only listed projects are managed. Omit it or use an empty list for none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mapping--organization_roles--project_roles))

<a id="nestedatt--mapping--organization_roles--project_roles"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mapping.organization_roles.project_roles`

Required:

- `project` (String) The project name. The project must exist in the organization.
- `role` (String) The built-in or custom project role name. The API does not check it, so a wrong name gives no error and sign-in skips the role.

## Import

The instance has one group mapping, so the import ID is always `instance`:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_group_mappings.this
  id = "instance"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# The instance has one group mapping, so the import ID is always "instance".
terraform import 'logfire_group_mappings.this' "instance"
```
